stories.title: Apple Screen Sharing Pre-Auth RCE
stories.author: warez.sl0p.foo via fro
bullet_points: The news concerns a critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in Apple's Screen Sharing feature.
The vulnerability is described as a 'pre-auth' issue, meaning it could potentially be exploited without prior user authentication.
This represents a high-severity security flaw impacting Apple's ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function in NLP.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, suggesting a focus on accessible, state-of-the-art models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
Key associated technologies include transformers and safetensors, standard in modern NLP.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors) point to its technical implementation within the ML ecosystem.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving 8.9 million developers in the open models space.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for models.
The updated engine also enables models to generate higher quality responses.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, enhancing local AI execution on Apple hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The core value proposition is running AI tasks entirely on the user's own hardware.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: Addresses the critical 'trust and accountability gap' caused by undisclosed system prompts in commercial LLM applications.
Introduces AISPA (Artificial Intelligence System Prompt Assurance), a new user-centric framework for auditing these prompts.
Focuses on systematically examining system prompts to improve transparency and governance of AI behavior.

stories.title: KAISEN: Reproducible Subgroup Fairness Auditing for Clinical Risk Models
stories.author: Nishita Chavan
bullet_points: Introduces KAISEN, a comprehensive five-phase audit pipeline designed to rigorously test fairness in clinical risk models.
Addresses a critical gap where existing fairness audit components are often untested, leading to uncertainty about their reliability.
Covers the full lifecycle of fairness auditing, including subgroup stratification, disparity measurement, mechanism diagnostics, and drift monitoring.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Change2Task, a system designed to generate executable tasks for training and evaluating coding AI agents.
The system leverages repository history (merged pull requests) to create realistic, verifiable coding tasks.
Addresses the critical need for a continuous supply of high-quality, state-coupled data for scaling modern coding agents.

stories.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
stories.author: Geoff Keeling
bullet_points: Safety fine-tuning in LLMs inadvertently alters how models represent 'mindedness' in other entities.
The research shows that alignment techniques suppress models from attributing consciousness to themselves, animals, and objects.
The process of safety fine-tuning also correlates with a measurable reduction in the models' tendency toward spiritual beliefs.

stories.title: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?
stories.author: Raaz Dwivedi
bullet_points: Introduces ORCA-bench, a new benchmark designed to test LLM agents in a production-fidelity oncall setting.
Highlights the gap between LLMs' current coding abilities and the complex reasoning required for real-world Root Cause Analysis (RCA).
The benchmark utilizes a live, OpenTelemetry-instrumented microservice system to simulate noisy, real-world incident data (metrics, logs, traces).

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models and hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance the knowledge base and real-time capability of Claude Code.

stories.title: As Reddit stock falls, CEO questions value of Google's AI Overviews
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Reddit is reportedly re-evaluating its licensing agreement with Google.
The uncertainty is linked to the recent performance and perceived value of Google's AI Overviews feature.
The situation highlights ongoing tension between content providers and major AI developers regarding data usage and compensation.

stories.title: Defcon's new badge is a security key you can see inside
stories.author: Kim Zetter, wired.com
bullet_points: Defcon's new security badges incorporate a visible, removable chip.
This design allows malicious actors to inspect the badge's contents.
The chip's nature permits hackers to retain and reuse the badge after the event.

stories.title: Google plans to exempt sanctioned nations from Android developer verification
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is planning to exempt sanctioned nations from Android developer verification requirements.
This change allows developers in countries like Cuba or Iran to continue installing APKs without new restrictions.
The policy shift is expected to negatively impact developers operating in these sanctioned regions.

stories.title: Reddit keeps its strange DMCA fight over Google search results alive
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Reddit is involved in a legal dispute concerning DMCA rights.
The lawsuit specifically targets Perplexity AI.
The core of the dispute involves allegations of conspiracy with a web scraper.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance degradation issues in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) when handling long visual contexts.
It introduces a single learnable embedding trained as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from the KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks despite being trained on a small dataset.

stories.title: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball
stories.author: Aaron D. Ames
bullet_points: Introduces PAC-MAN, a novel Perception-Aware Control Barrier Function Reinforcement Learning (CBF-RL) framework.
Addresses whole-body safety in humanoid robotics during dynamic tasks like dodgeball.
Combines realistic onboard sensing (segmentation-masked depth) with comprehensive training-time safety guidance.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem introduces a new infrastructure for chemistry literature synthesis, moving beyond simple document ranking.
It shifts the unit of retrieval from the entire paper to specific, provenance-carrying claims within the literature.
This aims to solve the current bottleneck where researchers must manually assemble scattered findings across multiple publications.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper introduces OSReward to standardize the evaluation of Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
Current CUA evaluation relies heavily on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) as automated judges for agent trajectories.
OSReward addresses the fundamental need for scalable and standardized verification of whether CUAs fulfill task instructions.

stories.title: PAIChecker: Uncovering and Checking PR-Issue Misalignment in SWE-Bench-Like Benchmarks
stories.author: Pinjia He
bullet_points: The paper introduces PAIChecker to address misalignment issues in PR-Issue pairings used in LLM evaluation benchmarks like SWE-Bench.
Current benchmarks rely on pairing PRs and issues, using the issue description as the problem and the PR patch as the oracle.
The core problem identified is that these pairings are often misaligned due to the complexity of maintaining large software repositories.

stories.title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
stories.author: Jianxin Li
bullet_points: The paper introduces DualG-MRAG to address limitations in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MM-RAG) for complex reasoning.
Existing MM-RAG methods struggle with multi-hop reasoning because they rely on independent instance-level matching.
The proposed method aims to decouple macro-reasoning from micro-matching to better capture cross-modal relationships while mitigating graph expansion issues.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend in LLM prompting where self-refinement and reflection methods (like Reflexion) are assumed to be superior.
It demonstrates that simple repeated sampling of the same prompt, at equal token cost, can outperform complex self-correction mechanisms.
The finding suggests that the benefit of increased output length itself, rather than the planning/reflection mechanism, may be driving accuracy gains in some scenarios.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance degradation issues in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) when handling long visual contexts.
The method introduces a single learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from the KV cache.
ReToken demonstrates consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks using only a small image-QA dataset.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem introduces a claim-centered infrastructure to address limitations in traditional chemistry literature search.
It moves beyond simple ranked document lists by focusing on retrieving specific, provenance-carrying claims across multiple papers.
This aims to automate the manual process scientists currently use to assemble cross-paper answers from scattered findings.

stories.title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
stories.author: Md. Umar Faruk
bullet_points: Introduces MixFrag, a novel mixed-precision Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) framework specifically for Vision Transformers (ViTs).
Addresses the limitation of uniform bit-width quantization by recognizing the heterogeneous sensitivity of different transformer components to quantization errors.
Aims to improve deployment efficiency of ViTs on resource-constrained devices through intelligent, fragility-guided precision allocation.

stories.title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the practical brittleness of On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) in improving reasoning language models.
It introduces $\beta$-OPSD, framing OPSD as a specific case ($\beta=1$) within a broader policy-optimization family.
The key contribution is making the KL penalty weight ($\beta$) a controllable parameter rather than a fixed value.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend of complex self-refinement methods (like Reflexion) in LLMs.
It suggests that simple repeated sampling of a prompt at equal token cost can outperform sophisticated planning/reflection techniques.
The finding implies that increased output length itself may be a primary driver of accuracy gains, rather than the complexity of the reasoning process.

stories.title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems
stories.author: Yatao Bian
bullet_points: Introduces APO, an unsupervised method for 3D structure prediction of atomic systems.
Addresses the bottleneck of expensive, supervised labeling required by existing flow-matching models (like FlowDPO).
Aims to enable structural modeling in data-scarce regimes, benefiting material science and drug discovery.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem is a new infrastructure designed to improve chemistry literature synthesis by moving beyond simple document retrieval.
It shifts the unit of retrieval from the entire paper to specific, provenance-carrying claims within the literature.
This addresses the current bottleneck where scientists must manually assemble scattered findings from multiple publications.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: The paper addresses the lack of transparency regarding system prompts, which govern LLM behavior in commercial AI.
It introduces AISPA (Artificial Intelligence System Prompt Assurance), a new framework for auditing these hidden system prompts.
The work aims to bridge the trust and accountability gap created by undisclosed AI instructions.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper introduces OSReward, a framework for standardizing the evaluation of Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
Evaluating CUA trajectories (actions, states, reasoning) is crucial but difficult to scale using human verification.
The research addresses the growing reliance on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) as automated judges for CUA performance.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Change2Task is a system designed to generate executable tasks for training and evaluating coding AI agents.
It leverages repository history, specifically merged pull requests, to create these tasks.
The system ensures tasks are grounded in realistic software states, development tools, and verification.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend of using complex self-refinement and reflection techniques in LLMs.
It suggests that simple repeated sampling of the same prompt can achieve comparable or better accuracy than elaborate multi-step reasoning methods.
The finding implies that the increased output length from complex methods might be artificially inflating perceived performance gains.

stories.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Kaiyan Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Frontis-MA1, an AI4AI model designed to pursue recursive self-improvement (RSI) within machine learning engineering.
Presents OpenMLE, an open full-stack system providing a concrete testbed for RSI research, including environments (OpenMLE-Gym), RL (OpenMLE-RL), and evolutionary search (OpenMLE-Evo).
The research focuses on enabling AI systems to improve the very process of building AI, a key long-term goal in advanced AI development.

stories.title: RFC 10015: Deprecating Obsolete Key Exchange Methods in TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2
stories.author: Jimmc414
bullet_points: RFC 10015 formalizes the deprecation of outdated key exchange methods within TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2.
This update is a crucial step in enhancing the cryptographic security posture of internet communications.
It signals an industry-wide move away from vulnerable or obsolete cryptographic protocols.

stories.title: CISA Alert: Water Sector PLC Targeting
stories.author: speckx
bullet_points: CISA has issued an alert regarding targeted threats.
The attack vector is specifically focused on the Water Sector.
This indicates a critical cybersecurity threat to essential infrastructure.

stories.title: The Shape of Failure: Before You Blame the AI
stories.author: copyleftdev
bullet_points: AI project failures are rarely singular events, suggesting systemic issues.
The article proposes using data contracts and agent boundaries to pinpoint failure origins.
Advanced testing methods like property-based and mutation testing are highlighted as diagnostic tools for AI systems.

stories.title: Designing Edit Operations for AI Agents
stories.author: gimalay
bullet_points: Focuses on the technical challenge of designing edit operations for AI agents.
Draws lessons from building a block-editing language specifically for LLM writers.
Highlights practical engineering considerations like defining the 'blast radius' of edits.
